events.title: Yukihiro Matsumoto releases Ruby 1.0
events.summary: Yukihiro 'Matz' Matsumoto released Ruby 1.0 on December 25, 1996 — crystallizing a language designed for programmer happiness.
events.about: Ruby's expressiveness influenced Rails, Elixir, and modern scripting language design. Matz built a global community from Japan that proved language innovation need not come from Silicon Valley.

narrative.whyChosen: Ruby 1.0 marked Matz's language graduating from personal project to production use.
narrative.whyImportant: It brought an object-oriented scripting alternative to Perl and Python with a distinct philosophy.
narrative.problemSolved: Developers wanted a more human-readable language without sacrificing object-oriented power.

events.title: CSS Level 1 becomes a W3C Recommendation
events.summary: The W3C published Cascading Style Sheets, Level 1 as an official Recommendation on December 17, 1996 — co-authored by Håkon Wium Lie and Bert Bos.
events.about: CSS1 let authors set fonts, colors, margins, and spacing in a separate stylesheet while readers could override styles through the cascade. A single linked `.css` file could style an entire site — ending the era of `<font>` tags and presentational HTML attributes in professional publishing.

narrative.whyChosen: CSS1 was the first stable web standard for separating document structure from presentation.
narrative.whyImportant: It gave browsers and authors a shared vocabulary for layout and typography on the open web.
narrative.problemSolved: HTML had no standard way to style pages consistently without polluting markup with presentation tags.
